# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1: THE WORLD MASTERS (George Griffith, 1903, John Long; Gutenberg 38028)

**Front matter:** Title, author; "Author of The Angel of the Revolution, Brothers of the Chain, The Justice of Revenge, A Honeymoon in Space, Captain Johnnie." Publisher John Long, 13–14 Norris Street, Haymarket, London, 1903. Ad catalogue at end lists Sidelights on Convict Life, Mrs Campbell Praed, Florence Warden, May Crommelin, Lucas Cleeve, Richard Marsh, etc.

**PROLOGUE "The Moment of Triumph":** Strassburg, night, old Fisher's Gate, River Ill. Dr Emil Fargeau (~60, tall, stooped, iron-grey hair, Alsatian patois) in attic laboratory. Machine: round, 3 ft, glass cylinder, four glass supports, batteries, silk-covered wires; a 4-inch steel plate under a ring of needles. Clock with wooden cuckoo. He strikes steel with wooden mallet; it shatters "as though glass." Speech: Germany the oppressor; France to rule world; "Soul of the World, Living Principle of Material Things"; Prince of Condé to sit on throne; Adelaide and Victor to rule. He has ten twenty-mark gold pieces (~£10), ~25 marks more. Jew Weinthal, a draft with a month to run; he altered figures to deceive him.

**CHAPTER I (27 Jan, Kaiser's birthday, German Embassy, Nevski Prospekt, Petersburg):** Prince Louis Xavier de Condé, Duc de Montpensier (~50, Bourbon features, Order of St Vladimir, Golden Fleece; refuses French orders, hates Republic). Daughter Adelaide de Condé, Marquise de Montpensier (<21, "Marie Antoinette replica"). Captain Victor Fargeau, Uhlan, military attaché, ~28, blue eyes, bronze cheeks. Adelaide and Victor's secret bond; she says "Victor... you may hope for everything." French Ambassador absent (sent excuses; friction with Germany). Countess Sophie Valdemar (19, golden-bronze hair, pansy-blue eyes, sensuous mouth), daughter of Count Leo Valdemar, Chief of Third Section, Ministry of Interior; "most skilful diplomatic detective in Europe." Sophie jealous of Adelaide. Victor says a lacquey summoned him. In winter garden Victor tells Adelaide "he had succeeded... goes to Paris to-morrow." Sophie overhears partly; vows to learn who and why Paris.

**CHAPTER II (Paris, Ministry of War):** Dr Emil Fargeau, late Prof. of Physics, Strassburg University, sees French Minister of War (unnamed in ch.II; later General Ducros). Minister refuses, demands demonstration; mentions Gulf Stream diversion scheme; "Pfennige." Minister offers 50-franc note; Fargeau refuses charity: "Tant pis pour toi." Fargeau has <100 francs; hotel in Paris. Had destroyed essential accumulator parts before leaving. Letters: to Victor (Petersburg), to Reuss Weinthal (Judenstrasse, Strassburg), and a letter with specifications sealed in air-tight tin case, tied to his body under coat. Takes Nord Station, second-class to Southampton via le Havre. At midnight in mid-channel, slips overboard; screw mangles him; tin box lashed to body floats.

**CHAPTER III (May, yacht Nadine, Channel between Guernsey and Southampton):** Ernest Shafto Hardress, Viscount Branston, eldest son of Earl of Orrel; with Frank Lamson, M.A. Cambridge, D.Sc. London (32). Body spotted; quarter-boat (mate Mr Jackson). Ladies: Lady Olive (~25, Irish eyes, Hardress's sister) and Miss Chrysie Vandel (daughter of Clifford K. Vandel, President, American Electrical Storage Trust, Buffalo, N.Y.). Chrysie quotes Kipling "Seven Seas"; "Inopportune, shrill-accented." Tin box taken; Lamson opens it.

**CHAPTER IV (cabin):** Lamson reads papers, locked door; monologues; "You infernal scoundrel!" Hides papers in hip-pocket. Tempted. Tells Hardress: "How would you like to be master of the world?" Describes: soak up earth's electricity; boilers burst, ships electrolised. Hardress enthusiastic; Vandel would back it; Morgan Steel Trust mentioned.

**CHAPTER V (Orrel Court, South Downs overlooking Solent):** Earl of Orrel (Harry Shafto Hardress, eighth Earl, 50s, widower; dead American wife's millions). Clifford K. Vandel, "Lightning King," tall, iron-grey moustache, Southern descent. Dinner: scheme discussed. Syndicate to be International Magnetic Control Syndicate. Lamson: "a little too splendid for human responsibility." Vandel: "Masters of the world..."

**CHAPTER VI:** Trip home in Nadine. Vandel president/financial manager. Lamson to study US electrical machinery. Hardress to Montreal; leases few sq miles of Boothia Felix (Boothia Land) at $1,000/yr for 10 years from Dominion Government; observatory cover story (Northern Lights, wireless). Hardress proposes to Chrysie at Buffalo; she: "I'm not going to say 'Yes' right away"; kiss on hand, "syllabus" joke, "territory... reserve"; "taken by assault." Vandel approves. Ship at Sandy Hook. Simultaneously Prince and Adelaide heading to Elsenau.

**CHAPTER VII (Elsenau, Thuringia; Hôtel Wilhelmshof, spring of gout/rheumatism water):** Lord Orrel and Lady Olive meet Prince and Adelaide. Adelaide and Olive become friends. Prince and Orrel friends since Aix-les-Bains (six years). Prince's son: Victor's former story; Orrel's younger brother killed by communards.

**CHAPTER VIII:** Prince tells Orrel the Fargeau story; Orrel tells his (the Nadine body). Prince shouts "Mon Dieu... same!" Prince retires; daughter Adelaide tends him. Night: fever, madness hereditary; calls for Adelaide. Opiate given. Dies at sunrise, cerebral haemorrhage, cry "France! O ma belle France..." Resident physician certifies. Hardress arrives that evening.

**CHAPTER IX:** Funeral; Prince buried in ordinary brick grave on hillside under pines, not in France. Madame de Condé (aunt, Princess of Bourbon) brought from Vienna. Adelaide's private diary (padded Russia-leather, silver lock): writes about Victor, Hardress ("master of the world"), wonders about another woman.

**CHAPTER X:** Hardress and father talk (Chrysie: Hardress says "it's Chrysie Vandel"). Adelaide & Victor in Vienna (prince's hotel on Ringstrasse). Victor plans to resign commission, go to Paris, offer France the secret. She refuses further kiss.

**CHAPTER XI:** Victor resigns German commission; Gaston Leraulx (Ministry secretary). Victor and Adelaide visit Paris; Avenue Neuilly. Victor & Adelaide meet General Ducros (Minister of War). Count Valdemar and Sophie arrive; Sophie hints: Boothia Land leased by Anglo-American syndicate.

**CHAPTER XII:** Russian trapper and French-Canadian voyageur cabled details. Ducros realised error. Sophie and Count Valdemar dine with Ducros, arrange secret room in Ministry (Ducros' private apartment). Interview: Victor offers Polar expedition (two old warships, disguised guns) to take Boothia works. Russia to share.

**CHAPTER XIII (Cowes week, Orrel Court):** Chrysie vs Adelaide rivalry. Chrysie tells father Vandel; he suspects Polar expeditions are armed. Fifth chapter-level: Sophie, Adelaide. Night: Sophie with Count, planning.

**CHAPTER XIV:** Sophie seduces Edward Williams (second engineer of Nadine, inventor, bitter) for sabotage (sanding, grit). Plan: Vlodoya (Russian yacht) to overtake Nadine mid-Atlantic. Count raises "kidnapping." Chrysie cables Lamson.

**CHAPTER XV:** Storage Works at Port Adelaide, Cape Adelaide, Boothia Land. Large engines; absorber; Lamson; Austin Vandel (nephew, general manager). Pylons across Canada/Greenland/Iceland. Telegraph line through Rae Isthmus. Lamson decides "freeze them out"; orders president & friends to Boothia.

**CHAPTER XVI:** Adelaide learns Russian ice-breaker Ivan the Terrible; Sophie–Adelaide talk at Vandel's bungalow Cowes. Chrysie and Hardress discuss; Hardress tells false-ish news of German scandal (Lieutenant, French spy; Fargeau extradition). Sophie plots Adelaide's alliance; Victor's letter.

**CHAPTER XVII:** Sophie tempts Adelaide to betray Orrels; Adelaide agrees, swears; Sophie promises no harm to Hardress, Lord Orrel, Lady Olive, Chrysie's father spared? (Sophie swears "in name of Holy Russia" no harm to viscount/father/sister). Chrysie suspicious.

**CHAPTER XVIII:** Sophie & Count aboard Vlodoya at Cherbourg. Telegram: "Dépêchez." Hardress: Nadine sails evening; Adelaide's maid Felice telegraphs; Chrysie intercepts. Edward Williams bribed.

**CHAPTER XIX:** Nadine sails at 20 knots; Williams summoned; Adelaide, Chrysie, Olive on bridge. Council: president says Vlodoya will catch them; gun to be mounted.

**CHAPTER XX:** Vandelite guns mounted (liquid gas frozen dynamite). Adelaide & Chrysie conversation: Chrysie's revolver (Smith & Wesson five-shooter). Williams caught sanding driving rod, shaft gritted; Nadine down to eight knots. Plan: play "lame duck"; let Vlodoya fire first.

**CHAPTER XXI:** Punch "à le Grand Monarque" brewed by Adelaide; drugs all aboard; Chrysie suspects and avoids. Captain Burgess, chief engineer M'Niven (Scottish), chief officer Mr Vernon, quartermasters. Vlodoya overtakes. Chrysie's Maxim.

**CHAPTER XXII:** Naval duel: Vandel's gun hits Vlodoya stern; Maxim; Vlodoya crippled. Chrysie with Maxim; shoots Vlodoya captain. Count and Sophie surrender.

**CHAPTER XXIII:** Vlodoya sunk; boats of crew set adrift; passengers aboard Nadine. Dinner; Chrysie fainted. Vlodoya sunk by Vandel gun. Nadine sets course to Boothia Land.

**CHAPTER XXIV:** Newspapers; French liner picks up Vlodoya boats. Germany demands Fargeau's extradition; France refuses; Triple Alliance mobilises. Trust circular (capitation fee $1/man/week; one week deadline; "electrical force" cut off). European powder-keg. 

**CHAPTER XXV:** Trust starts engines (Chrysie pulls lever at 6). Engines purr; Adelaide & Sophie remark. Charles Martel (French battleship) disabled; German Brunsbüttel fort guns burst; compasses erratic; Kiel communication dead.

**CHAPTER XXVI:** Universal breakdown in Europe; guns burst, lances splinter, locomotives fail; French President Loubet and Kaiser (Wilhelm) sail to England; meet at Claridge's; Marlborough House with King Edward; Kaiser: "We are beaten." Mediation by King Edward accepted. Russian ice-breaker and French squadron arrive at Boothia.

**CHAPTER XXVII:** Hostile squadrons: Ivan the Terrible, Admiral Alexis Nazanoff; French: Vice-Admiral Dumont, Victor Fargeau (scientific command). Count and Sophie; Sophie & Adelaide; Adelaide takes Chrysie's revolver (pickpocketed by Sophie). Invitation to dinner.

**CHAPTER XXVIII:** Tea party: Chrysie's seven-shooter. Message from King Edward (Edward R.I.): powers accept arbitration. Lord Orrel and Count to port; electric car. Dinner in board-room; Professor Josef Karnina (Russian). Hardress declares "annihilated" threat.

**CHAPTER XXIX:** Victor claims the soul/power. Hardress: "you would be common pirates." Admirals grant truce till 6 a.m. Lady Olive plays "God Save the King," Sophie sings Russian hymn; Adelaide shoots at Chrysie/Hardress at farewell: Hardress's thigh broken; Chrysie arm/ear grazed; Sophie & Victor fire; Lamson's ray (disintegrator) kills Sophie, Adelaide, Victor to bones. Orrel's ear snipped; president's shoulder wounded.

**CHAPTER XXX:** Lord Orrel announces deaths; Admiral Nazanoff refuses to withdraw; Williams handcuffed, sent to ships; Count vows vengeance. Admiral Dumont: attack at six; count to fire first gun.

**CHAPTER XXXI:** Attack at 6: searchlights, death-ray; Count killed by ray on Ivan; Dumont's Caiman; ships destroyed; survivors return to Europe.

**CHAPTER XXXII (Epilogue? labelled EPILOGUE):** Hardress and Chrysie recover; Lady Olive nurses; Chrysie asserts claim; Hardress: "Buffalo's not Boothia." Doctor Lamson reports Powers surrendered; arbitration: Pope, Archbishop of Canterbury, Archimandrite. Chrysie: "We four... run the world." Kiss. Catalogue ad pages follow.

## BOOK 2: THE ROMANCE OF GOLDEN STAR (George Griffith[-Jones], Arno Press reprint 1978; Gutenberg 20173)

**Frontispiece:** "Hail, Son of the Sun!" Illustrated by Alfred Pearse. Prophecy epigraph: Son of the Sacred Race who, for Honour, Faith and Love, takes hand of pure virgin of holy blood, passes through Gate of Death; raises Rainbow Banner over Golden Throne of the Incas (Vilcaroya-Inca and Golden Star, sister-bride). Published London: F.V. White & Co, 1897.

**PROLOGUE I: "His Highness the Mummy":** Professor Martin Lamson (South American archaeologist, Maida Vale house) and Dr Laurens Djama (physiologist, ~32, Eastern look, Brondesbury Park). Mummy: Inca prince, lying flat (unusual), ~3 centuries old, dull brown long hair, bronze skin, unembalmed. Found 4 days' ride west of Cuzco, valley with lake, under overhanging ledge; cave with stone wall; arriero Patricio. Taken via Arequipa, Mollendo steamer. Djama proposes resuscitation; bargain: half of treasure. Calls it a pact with "Mephistopheles."

**PROLOGUE II: "A Physiological Experiment":** Djama's laboratory (Kilburn). Mummy revived; Lamson faints. Inca wakes: "Am I only dreaming that the death-sleep is over?" Name Vilcaroya-Inca; wife Golden Star (Nusta mi, Cori-Coyllur). Aymaru dialect of Quichua. Tradition of death-bridal. Vilcaroya insists on finding Golden Star.

**CHAPTER I (Back Through the Shadows):** Vilcaroya narrates. Ruth Djama (Joyful Star, sister of Djama) named by him Cusi-Coyllur. Francis Hartness (English captain, ~30, blue eyes, golden hair). Party via Panama, Arequipa (Misti volcano), Sicuani, Cacha, Piquillacta, Cuzco. Vilcaroya vows vengeance.

**CHAPTER II (Brothers of the Blood):** Village San Sebastian; Ullullo (old Indian) and Tupac-Rayca (chief, great-grandson of Tupac-Amaru). Oath: 20 men of the Blood. Hacienda price 20,000 soles (£2,000). Djama sneers. Joyful Star: "Vilcaroya is our friend." Vilcaroya claims Golden Star as sister & wife; Ruth horrified; Hartness and professor explain incest taboo; Ruth leaves.

**CHAPTER III (In the Hall of Gold):** Vilcaroya follows Djama (Ullullo paid $10 to spy). Rodadero, Sayacusca (Tired Stone), cleft, hidden copper chain, underwater tunnel, 50 steps, silver socket, great slab door. Hall of Gold with golden plates, gold ingot pyramid, sun-images with diamond eyes. Vilcaroya dresses in imperial robes (Huascar's). Binds Djama blindfold. Sells gold for hacienda.

**CHAPTER IV (The Sister Stars):** Five-day journey; Saljantai, Umantai, Lima Tambo, Apurimac bridge. Hidden tunnel to Golden Star's tomb (lake). Ruth and Golden Star resemble each other. Vilcaroya's love shifts to Ruth. Tomb opened; Golden Star's body.

**CHAPTER V (How Djama Did His Work):** Djama revives Golden Star in locked laboratory. Djama confesses love; demands Golden Star; threatens Ruth. Vilcaroya points dagger; Djama yields: "My sister for your sister."

**CHAPTER VI (Waking of Golden Star):** Ruth ends the threat; Ruth rebukes both men. Golden Star awakes with blank memory, child-like mind. Vilcaroya and Hartness become brothers-in-arms. Hartness plans civil war; Peru's government weak.

**CHAPTER VII (Throne-room of Yupanqui):** Ruth nurses Golden Star. Djama asks payment; Vilcaroya's oath of secrecy. Djama wants to take Golden Star to England. Vilcaroya asks Ruth into Hall of Gold; she is shown the throne room; Vilcaroya proposes to Ruth (Joyful Star) on throne-room kneeling.

**CHAPTER VIII (Soul of Golden Star Comes Back):** Gathering of 60 heads of Ayllos; Vilcaroya proclaimed Inca; Golden Star recognises Vilcaroya; Vilcaroya declares Joyful Star his Coya. Djama plots with Spanish officer; Hartness leads.

**CHAPTER IX (Treachery of Djama):** Djama betrays to Governor Antonio Prada of Cuzco (son Coronel Prada, Spanish officer). Vilcaroya traps Spanish officer and Djama in Hall of Gold; both walled into golden cells. Djama bribes; gold-madness.

**CHAPTER X (On the Rodadero):** Vilcaroya kills sentry with knife; Hartness disguised. Sentries captured. Anahuac, Ainu, Tupac sympathise.

**CHAPTER XI (How We Took the City of the Sun):** Governor Prada and officers trapped in water-cavern; surrender. Two machine-guns at cathedral; Hartness leads charge. Cuzco taken; Cuartel secured.

**CHAPTER XII (Queen and Crown):** Joyful Star addresses; Djama's voice from cell pleads for Ruth. Vilcaroya proposes; Ruth accepts: "Your queen is not crowned yet." Ruth gives Golden Star's hand to Hartness. Coronation at Sun temple; Rainbow Banner flies; Vilcaroya proclaimed Inca.

**CHAPTER XIII (How Djama Paid His Debt):** Djama tries to shoot Vilcaroya; Ullullo killed by Djama's rifle shot; Djama poisons/chokes himself dead.

**CHAPTER XIV (Re-kindling of the Sacred Fire):** Empire restored from Lima; Feast of Raymi; Tupac-Rayca high priest (Villac-Umu); Hartness called Viracocha. Prophecy repeated. Sacred fire re-kindled. Marriage font: wine and water; Vilcaroya and Joyful Star wed; Golden Star and Hartness wed.

**FOOTNOTES:** Footnotes on Inca customs, Llautu, Borla, Coya, Church of Santo Domingo (not Cathedral); List of corrections (Anahauc→Anahuac, ont→out, Ullulo→Ullullo).
